newsitem.title: USA: Better compliance with muni rules needed-MSRB.
newsitem.headline: Better compliance with muni rules needed-MSRB.

text.p: Some municipal bond dealers are not complying with MSRB transaction reporting rules and enforcement agencies are monitoring the problem, a market regulator said Thursday.

"We're looking at it and the National Association of Securities Dealers is looking at it," Hal Johnson, deputy general counsel of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, said at a Public Securities Association conference here.

Under the MSRB's price transparency pilot system, muni dealers already should be reporting prices in interdealer trades and beginning in January 1998 they must report trades with institutional and retail customers.
"The reports need to be correct," Johnson said.

"How many advisories are we stamping?" he said, referring to dealers. "How many as-of transactions are we putting in? How many times are we deleting trades after we are putting them in? And are we putting the name of the executing broker in correctly?" he said.
"This is an area where we do see some noncompliance," Johnson said.

Johnson noted that MSRB will begin testing the next round of price transparency requirements as early as July 1997. "You should be thinking about this because it is going to take some preparation by your firm," Johnson said.

"In essence, you'll have to produce a file every night of customer transactions in municipal securities. And you'll have to get that file to MSRB by midnight. We plan to begin testing July 1997," he said.

Turning to the MSRB's political contribution rules g-37 and g-38, Johnson said that dealers need to make sure the quarterly forms that they file with regulators under the standards are "complete and timely."
"The NASD is checking and sending letters to people who have failed to get forms in on time," Johnson said.
Johnson also said dealers should describe offerings in as much detail as possible, including the six-digit CUSIP number.
Johnson also said that a lot of forms that dealers must send the MSRB under the board's rule g-36 "are coming in late."
"People are looking at this," Johnson said, referring to regulators. "There has got to be a checklist. You should have a tickler system."
